conviction_note: A modest long lean. The 10-Q member count (1,091k at June 30, up from 1,025k at March 31), together with management's 'roughly flat revenue per member' framing, implies Q3 revenue near $89-91M against a $85.8M consensus. The company has also raised its full-year guide every quarter, and the short base grew into the print. But the name's reaction to beats is two-sided (Q1 beat-and-raise -9.6%, Q2 beat-and-raise +21%), and 2027 GLP-1 coverage commentary is the swing factor. So p_up is held at 58 on an abs move of 9, which scales to +1.44, about half the +2.7 findings sum. The gap is the reaction-function veto, not an inconsistency.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $85.8M and non-GAAP EPS about $0.09 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-10-28, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/OMDA/22353). Benzinga's table has $85.7M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/OMDA/earnings-forecasts); Yahoo's range is $84.5-86.4M; FXEmpire shows $87.39M (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/omda/earnings). The Earnings Whispers whisper is $0.12 EPS. Company guide: FY2026 revenue $334-340M and adj. EBITDA $21-27M (Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001611115/000162828026054266/q2fy26pressrelease.htm). With H1 at $165.8M (Q1 $78.0M + Q2 $87.8M), that implies H2 of $168.2-174.2M, about $84-87M a quarter, so consensus sits inside the guide. No quarterly guide is given. Two estimate sources agree, so the bar is treated as sourced.
positioning_check: Short interest is 8.35M shares as of the 2026-10-15 FINRA settlement, 6.7 days to cover on 1.24M average daily volume, about 13.6% of 61.22M shares outstanding and a higher share of float (https://massive.com/quote/omda). It was 7.45M / 4.4 DTC at 2026-09-30, so the short base was building into the print. The option chain is unusable (ATM spread 120% of mid), with no skew. Put/call OI is 1.9 on only 505 contracts, which is not meaningful. ATM IV is 102.6%, realised vol 79.8%. The stock is -11.7% over 20 days and -26% from its 52-week high, sitting near its post-Q2 low of $17.48 (Earnings Whispers). Bearish sentiment rose to 24.7% from 22.2%. Net read: the stock is de-rated into the print with a moderately crowded, growing short, which argues against sizing any negative large.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q puts total members at 1,091k on June 30, 2026 (1,025k on March 31; 752k a year earlier). Q2 revenue of $87.8M was about $83 per average member per quarter, and the Q1 call said revenue per member should be roughly flat for the rest of 2026. Holding members flat to slightly up through Q3 (seasonally a low-enrollment quarter, but billed monthly in arrears, so H1 enrollments carry forward) gives Q3 revenue of about $89-91M, against a $85.8M consensus that implies a sequential decline from $87.8M. A beat of about +4% looks likely, and with the H2 guide implying only $84-87M a quarter, a third consecutive FY raise looks likely too.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats with FY raises got both reactions. Q1 2026: $78.05M vs about $74.1M consensus (+5.3%) plus a raise, and the stock fell 9.6% (baseline 2026-05-07; biopharmawatch day-0 -9.6%). Q2 2026: $87.8M vs $80.9M (+8.5%) plus a raise, and it rose 21.1% (baseline 2026-08-06). Q3 2025: -7.1%; Q4 2025: +3.3%. Beats are not reliably bought; the size of the beat and the forward commentary decided it.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus ($85.7-85.8M from two sources) sits below Q2's $87.8M and inside a guide that implies flat-to-down quarters. If the market had priced the member-count arithmetic, consensus would be at or above $88M, and the stock would not be near its post-Q2 low with short interest rising 12% in two weeks.
findings.independence: The flat-revenue-per-member framing is from a different document, the Q1 call coverage (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/omada-health-q1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-05-08/). The beat-and-raise pattern (guide raised from $312-322M to $322-330M to $334-340M) is from the Q2 8-K and the Earnings Whispers preview. The 10-Q member count and the 8-K revenue are one company's own documents, so this is one finding. Counterweight: Q2 may have carried catch-up revenue billed in arrears, and management explicitly guided slower H2 growth on seasonality and tough comps.

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 7.45M (2026-09-30, 4.4 DTC) to 8.35M (2026-10-15, 6.7 DTC), about 13.6% of shares outstanding, while the stock fell 11.7% in 20 days to near its post-Q2 low. Bears are building into a print whose recent pattern is beat-and-raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, with the stock de-rated into the print, a beat-and-raise produced +21.1%, the name's largest reaction. There is no prior short-interest series tied to the prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price. What it adds is the asymmetry: a beat forces covering at 6.7 days to cover. If shorts were already covering, the 20-day tape would be firm rather than -11.7%.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/OMDA/22353): bearish sentiment up to 24.7% from 22.2%, and the stock near its $17.48 post-earnings low. Different source, same direction.

findings.finding: Peer Hinge Health (employer and health-plan digital health, same buyers) reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-02: revenue $235.0M, +52% YoY, a 'record sales season', client count +28% to 3,270, and FY2026 revenue guide raised to $879-881M. It spoke after Omada last did, and points to healthy employer demand for digital programs going into the 2027 benefit year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of OMDA trading on Hinge prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Hinge's print was public three days before OMDA's, and OMDA did not rally on it (-6.4% over 5 days). It is a proxy for the selling season, not Omada's own number.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, MSK rather than cardiometabolic. The Hinge 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001673743/000162828026068872/hnge-q32026112xex991.htm) is the same document as the source.

findings.finding: Employer GLP-1 coverage is retreating for 2027. Business Group on Health found about 10% of covering employers likely to drop coverage; Mercer found 5% of large employers plan to drop and 27% tightened criteria; Cigna/Evernorth saw a 'slight downtick' in clients covering GLP-1s. GLP-1 is Omada's fastest enrollment hook, so 2027 commentary on the call could disappoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print (-9.6%) came alongside GLP-1 channel news (Lilly Employer Connect) and coverage worries. There is no clean single-line history.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public since June and named in the preview as the key risk. What is unpriced is how Omada's own 2027 selling season came in. Omada offsets with cash-pay GLP-1 Flex Care, Lilly Employer Connect and three PBM pathways. Sized small because short interest is building against it.
findings.independence: Cigna 'slight downtick' (https://beckershospitalreview.com/glp-1s/cigna-sees-slight-downtick-in-evernorth-clients-covering-glp-1s) and Earnings Whispers naming the same risk. All are macro-to-company transmission that Omada has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Cigna affiliates are Omada's two largest channel partners (Partner A 31% and Partner B 33% of Q2 revenue; top five partners 79%). Cigna said in July that Evernorth PBM retention was above 97% for 2026, with preliminary indicators of mid-90s% or higher for 2027, so the channel carrying about two-thirds of Omada's revenue looks stable into next year.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since July. Its relevance to Omada comes through the 10-Q concentration disclosure, which few previews connect. Small.
findings.independence: The 10-Q concentration figures (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001611115/000162828026054840/omda-20260630.htm) are a different document from Cigna's call. The rebate-free Evernorth model from 2027 is a change whose effect on digital-health carve-ins is unknown.

findings.finding: Management guided H2 adj. EBITDA margins to about 7%, down from 12% in Q2, as hiring annualises. FY adj. EBITDA of $21-27M less H1 of $11.7M implies H2 of $9.3-15.3M, so a sequential EBITDA and EPS step-down is expected, and the headline EPS will look lower than Q2's.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior quarter with a guided margin step-down.
findings.why_not_priced: It lands inside the guide and consensus EPS of $0.09 already reflects it, so it is near zero. Filed so the panel sees the margin optics.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K EBITDA guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001611115/000162828026054266/q2fy26pressrelease.htm). Shares a premise with finding 1: a revenue beat would flow at high incremental margin.

findings.finding: This is the last print before the CEO change on January 1, 2027 (President Wei-Li Shao succeeds co-founder Sean Duffy, who becomes Executive Chair), and the first since Investor Day (2026-09-10), which set long-term targets of at least 20% revenue growth, 80% non-GAAP gross margin and 30% adj. EBITDA margin. The call may give early 2027 framing against a 20% floor, versus about 30% growth in 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No 2027 guide has been given; the company historically guides at the Q4 print in March and at JPM in January (baseline 2026-01-12 +4.6%).
findings.why_not_priced: Known since August and September. A formal 2027 guide is unlikely on this call. Zero-sized; filed for context.

The baseline flags cadence_implausible, but the six dates match real earnings releases: Q2 on 2026-08-06, Q1 on 2026-05-07 (biopharmawatch confirms -9.6%), Q4 on 2026-03-05, the JPM preliminary on 2026-01-12, and Q3/Q2 2025. The flag looks like an artefact of the January pre-announcement shortening the gap. abs_move was still set independently from 80% realised vol and the 21% max.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lilly Employer Connect and Optum Rx Weight Engage channel additions as a Q3 revenue driver
rejected_candidates.detail: Announced 2026-05-07. Its revenue effect is already inside the member and revenue-per-member arithmetic of finding 1, and management said the new programs are not material to 2026.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to read. The long lean runs against the -11.7% 20-day run-up and the rising short interest, which is the point: the market is de-rating a name whose own filings imply a beat. Because beats on this name have been sold as often as bought, p_up is held at 58 rather than 65.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Q3 revenue finding was cut from 2.5 to 2.0 because Q1's beat-and-raise sold off 9.6%, and p_up was moved from 60 to 58.
Lesson 5 (a proxy is filed small): the Hinge peer read was cut from 0.5 to 0.4.
Lesson 7 (a crowded short shrinks the negative): the GLP-1 coverage negative was cut from -1.0 to -0.8, given 8.35M shares short at 6.7 days to cover and rising.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): two agreeing sources ($85.8M and $85.7M) plus the company FY guide, so no cap was needed; the EBITDA step-down was kept near 0 because it lands inside the guide.

Lesson on reaction histories built from the wrong events: the baseline's history was checked against confirmed release dates and appears to be real earnings, but abs_move was not anchored on its median.
